headline: Rest day — and today the body agrees: sleep debt and a spiked resting HR say protect, don't push.
body_state: Readiness **51 (moderate)**, Garmin **Recovery**, overtraining flag **caution** — and the deterministic verdict is **red**: *"Sleep debt building — protect today."* Sleep last night **5.7 h** (score 59) on top of **23 h of 14-day debt**. The red driver is resting HR: **87 bpm vs a 45 baseline** — a big spike, so treat it as an early warning, not a verdict (hydrate, sleep). HRV **41 ms, balanced**, body battery **43**. Nothing here is broken, but everything points the same way: bank recovery today.
session: **No run on the calendar today — that's correct, take it.** The job is to clear sleep debt: aim for lights-out ~60 min earlier tonight. Tomorrow (Fri) is the **6 km long run**, the shortest of the plan on purpose — easy, no targets, watch stays quiet, run to feel. If resting HR is still elevated in the morning, keep it a true easy shuffle and don't chase the pace band. Any HYROX/strength work today stays genuinely easy — the cutback only works if the off-day load drops too.
recent: The theme of the last four days is **easy days that aren't easy enough** — your #1 limiter, live. Yesterday's treadmill 'easy' run was green on volume (5.5 km) but **64% of it sat in Zone 3** and it closed at 77% max HR — a moderate run dressed as a recovery run. The Salou holiday runs (Jul 17 & 19) were more defensible: 4:59–5:23/km in 23–24 °C heat and 78–86 m of hills kept HR honest at 135–143. Pattern: on flat, cool ground you drift into the grey zone; that's exactly what's costing recovery right now.
focus: Protect today — bed ~60 min earlier, hydrate; the 23 h sleep debt and RHR 87 are the story.
Tomorrow's long run: cap HR in zone 2 and start embarrassingly controlled — that fixes grey-zone drift and pacing in one move.
Rate any HYROX/strength session (RPE) so station load counts instead of vanishing.
